content: Any Zod schema handed to Codex/OpenAI as a structured-output response_format must have EVERY property in its `required` array, recursively — an `.optional()` field makes OpenAI reject the request with invalid_json_schema. Never leave a backend-stamped optional field (review_mode, provider, deliberation, session_id) in a model-facing *ResponseSchema; omit it. Because unit tests mock the SDK and the Gemini backend doesn't enforce this, such a break is INVISIBLE without a live Codex probe — verify structured-output schema changes against a real Codex call, and rely on the recursive required-covers-properties lock test in orchestrator.test.ts.
context: ISS-019 (fixed in T-029, commit badf79b): T-028 added review_mode (optional) to the *ResultSchema; the model-facing *ResponseSchema in orchestrator.ts omits backend-stamped fields but forgot review_mode, so toJSONSchema emitted it as non-required and OpenAI rejected every live Codex structured review (plan/code/precommit, single + deliberate). Masked all session because tests mock the SDK, Gemini doesn't enforce it (reviews degraded silently to Gemini-only), and Codex was rate-limited when T-028 landed. Discovered via a live deliberate-deep probe during T-029 Step 1. Probe-loop taxonomy: cross-layer trust violation + environment mismatch (correct vs mocked SDK, broken vs real validator).
title: Model-facing response schemas must have every property required (OpenAI structured outputs)
